To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of the hemagglutin HA2 and SV40 Vp1 peptides to NT-vector improves its ability to transfer plasmid DNA into NTRH-bearing cells.

the neurotensin-polylysine conjugate, which binds plasmid DNA and is taken up by cells expressing the high affinity neurotensin-receptor (NTRH), can be improved by the addition of viral fusogenic and karyophilic peptides.
the fusogenic peptide of hemagglutin HA2 and the karyophilic sequence of the SV40 Vp1 viral protein increase the transfection efficiency and the nuclear delivery of the neurotensin vector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a gene transfer system for the treatment of Parkinson's disease.
the development of a novel gene delivery system for the brain.
the development of an efficient gene transfer system for NTRH-bearing cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NT-polymer is a very efficient gene vector for gene delivery into NTRH-expressing cells, and the addition of the HA2 and Vp1 viral peptides to NT-polymer improves gene transfer.
the fusogenic and the karyophilic NT-polyplexes are highly efficient and specific neurotensin vectors.
the fusogenic and karyophilic peptides are able to increase the transfection of neurotensin vectors, but only when the neurotensin vector is able to bind to its receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusogenic and karyophilic peptides of the fusogenic-kariophilic-NT-vectored polyplex are essential for the improvement of neurotensin-mediated gene transfer.
the NT-vector can be improved in its transfecting properties by coupling the HA2 fusogenic and Vp1 karyophilic peptide to NT-polymer.
NT-polyplexes are able to transfer gene to dopamine neurons in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of neurotensin as a vector for the transfer of genes to neurons is feasible and efficient, and that the addition of fusogenic and karyophilic peptides to the neurotensin-polyplex increases transfection efficiency.
the NT-polyfusion system is a very efficient gene delivery system for NTRH-bearing cells.
the NT-vector is a promising gene delivery tool that can be used to target the dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigral.
